nuggets.title: ETA wrong after sudden road closure

scenario.symptoms: ETAs underestimated by 18 minutes across a corridor after bridge closure. Traffic feature pipeline still served pre-closure speeds for 45 minutes.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Online features refresh every 30 minutes from batch table; closure events not wired to streaming override.

incident.headline: Batch traffic features lagged real-world closure

agenda.goal: Pick and compute the features that drive each stage.
agenda.opener: Drivers routed into a closed bridge—the traffic feature path is highlighted. How do you freshness-fix ETAs?

evidence.strong: Prep: historical prep time by restaurant, item and hour, open orders in the kitchen now, recent prep-time trend; courier: available couriers nearby, assignment delays, routing time, traffic and weather; order size and type; drop-off difficulty; real-time ones from streams, the rest from batch.
evidence.adequate: Reasonable features without freshness or source.
evidence.weak: Distance and time of day only.

misconceptions.challenge: A restaurant usually takes twelve minutes, but has fifteen orders open right now. What's your estimate?

probes: How fresh must kitchen load be?
How do you handle a restaurant that never taps 'food ready'?
hints: What's happening right now beats last month.
Courier wait times reveal when food was really ready.
agenda.referenceFix: Stream closure and incident feeds into online store, lower TTL on corridor features, fallback to live probe data, and alert when feature age exceeds SLO.

scenario.symptoms: Complaints rose when meals arrived outside the 5-minute quoted window though model RMSE was fine. Interval always ±3 minutes regardless of route variance.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Serving returns point estimate with fixed margin; quantile model outputs ignored in API layer.

incident.headline: Fixed uncertainty band ignored route-specific variance

agenda.goal: Handle uncertainty and the asymmetric cost of lateness.
agenda.opener: Customers distrust ETAs—the uncertainty presentation path is highlighted. How should intervals work?

evidence.strong: Predicts quantiles (P50 and P80 or P90) with quantile loss, shows a range or a cautious point, chooses the displayed quantile through experiments balancing conversion against lateness, and checks quantile coverage.

misconceptions.challenge: If you show the average, how often is the delivery late?

probes: How would you choose which quantile to show?
How do you check the P90 is really a P90?
hints: A model can predict more than the middle.
Coverage tells you if the upper estimate is honest.
agenda.referenceFix: Serve p10/p90 from quantile model, widen on long routes and bad weather features, calibrate intervals to hit coverage targets, and show honest ranges in UI.

nuggets.title: Batch route matrix job timeouts at city scale

scenario.symptoms: Nightly ETA retrain failed after city expansion; all-pairs shortest path matrix exceeded memory on single Spark driver.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Matrix built globally in one stage without graph partitioning or hierarchical contraction.

incident.headline: Monolithic all-pairs matrix exceeded compute limits

agenda.goal: Afford estimates for many restaurants on every search.
agenda.opener: City scale broke the route matrix job—the search scale path is highlighted. How do you scale graph features?

evidence.strong: Computes the requests per second, caches estimates per restaurant and delivery area (for example a hexagon) for about a minute, batches model calls, precomputes for active restaurants, and reserves exact per-order predictions for checkout.
evidence.adequate: Caches results without keys or TTL reasoning.
evidence.weak: Calls the full model per restaurant per search.

misconceptions.pattern: Runs the full model for every restaurant on every search.
misconceptions.challenge: Tens of thousands of searches a second times dozens of restaurants: how many model calls is that?

probes: How stale can a search-page estimate be?
agenda.referenceFix: Partition graph by region, use contraction hierarchies or sampling for far pairs, incremental updates for changed edges, and distributed storage of blocks.

scenario.symptoms: Live ETA bias spiked after deploy though offline eval looked good. Serving hash encodes road segments differently than training pipeline after library upgrade.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Training uses Python 3.10 feature job; serving C++ encoder lags one version on polyline splitting.

incident.headline: Encoder version mismatch between train and serve

agenda.goal: Choose and train the models sensibly.
agenda.opener: Offline metrics fine but live ETAs biased—the train/serve path is highlighted. Where is skew?

evidence.strong: A baseline of routing time plus average prep, gradient-boosted trees per stage, possibly a deep model predicting the residual over the routing estimate; time-based splits and rolling backtests; regular retraining.
evidence.adequate: A reasonable model with no baseline or time split.

misconceptions.challenge: Training on next week's holiday rush to predict last week's: what goes wrong?

probes: What baseline must the model beat?
How do you split data for evaluation?
hints: Start with what the routing engine already gives you.
agenda.referenceFix: Shared feature spec artifact, contract tests on sample routes in CI, shadow compare train vs serve outputs, and block deploy on skew alerts.

nuggets.title: ETA drift went unalerted for two weeks

scenario.symptoms: Mean absolute error crept up 30% over two weeks after map vendor change. Monitoring dashboard only tracked p95 latency not error vs actuals.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Ground truth feedback loop broken when trip completion events stopped emitting to metrics topic.

incident.headline: Missing ground-truth feed left accuracy unmonitored

agenda.goal: Detect bad estimates quickly and degrade safely.
agenda.opener: ETAs got worse but nobody noticed—the monitoring path is highlighted. What should alert?

evidence.strong: Live dashboards of error and lateness by city and stage, alerts on spikes, feature-freshness checks on the streams, a conservative buffer or fallback when inputs look abnormal, and incidents feeding retraining.

misconceptions.pattern: Checks accuracy only in weekly reports.
misconceptions.challenge: Estimates are twenty minutes late tonight in one city. When does a weekly report notice?

probes: What would you show if the model's inputs are broken?
agenda.referenceFix: Stream actual vs predicted into error metrics by segment, alert on drift, page when feedback pipeline stalls, and weekly calibration reviews.
